subject: Physics
description: Sound speed, pitch vs loudness, Doppler effect, ultrasonics

questions.explanation: Sound is a mechanical wave — needs a medium with vibrating particles. No medium → no propagation. That's why in space (vacuum) astronauts communicate via radio (electromagnetic waves), not sound. Speed order: solids > liquids > gases (denser elasticity transmits faster).
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The approximate speed of sound in AIR at 20 °C is:
questions.explanation: Speed of sound in air at 20 °C ≈ 343 m/s. In water ≈ 1500 m/s. In steel ≈ 5000 m/s. 3 × 10⁸ m/s is the speed of light in vacuum — the lightning-before-thunder rule exploits this huge gap.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: The PITCH of a sound depends on its:
questions.explanation: Higher frequency → higher pitch (treble); lower frequency → lower pitch (bass). Amplitude determines LOUDNESS. Speed of sound is a property of the medium, not the wave. Human hearing: 20 Hz to 20 kHz.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: Ultrasonic > 20 kHz (beyond human hearing). Uses: medical imaging (sonography), SONAR (fish-finders, submarines), cleaning, non-destructive testing. Infrasonic < 20 Hz (elephants and whales use it). Bats use ultrasonic echolocation.
questions.subject: Physics

options.option_text: The pitch of an approaching ambulance siren is HIGHER and drops as it recedes

questions.explanation: Apparent frequency changes when source and observer are in relative motion. Approach → wavefronts compressed → higher observed frequency (pitch). Recede → stretched → lower pitch. Astronomical red-shift is the Doppler effect for light — how we know the universe is expanding.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.stem: An ECHO is produced when sound is reflected from a distant surface and returned. For a distinct echo to be heard, the minimum distance from the reflector should be approximately (speed of sound = 340 m/s, persistence of hearing = 0.1 s):
questions.explanation: Sound must travel to the reflector AND back within 0.1 s for the echo to be distinct from the original. Round-trip distance ≥ 340 × 0.1 = 34 m. One-way distance ≥ 17 m.
questions.subject: Physics

questions.explanation: In gases and liquids, sound is longitudinal — particles oscillate parallel to the direction of wave propagation, creating compressions and rarefactions. Transverse sound can exist only in solids (shear waves) — in S-waves from earthquakes.
